newsitem.title: CHINA: China, General Motors in $1.3 bln car deal.
newsitem.headline: China, General Motors in $1.3 bln car deal.

text.p: General Motors Corp and the state-owned Shanghai Automotive Industry Corp have agreed on a $1.3 billion joint venture to produce cars in Shanghai, White House officials said on Tuesday.
The $1.3 billion joint venture will be held equally between General Motors and the Chinese side, the officials said.
The Shanghai-based joint venture will produce Buick Century sedans and Regal automobiles and will build car engines and transmissions, officials said.
GM has said it expects plant production to begin with 100,000 medium-sized Buick sedans a year and eventually to increase capacity to 300,000.
The agreement is to be signed by General Motors chairman Jack Smith and an official of Shanghai Automotive, and witnessed by visiting U.S. Vice President Al Gore.
